conceptZh: 披風英雄想把禮物給朋友，但他的長披風一直把禮物捲走、蓋住他的頭，最後披風乖乖放開，禮物和「給」字一起遞出去。
object: a caped action-figure hero with a too-long red cape, and a ribbon-tied gift box
morph: the cape hands over strands that form 糸 and 合 as the gift lands, making 給
creativeAngle: 道具反抗：披風不聽話，三次把禮物捲走或蓋住英雄的頭，英雄用打結治住它，才把「糸」與「合」交給對方。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with a locked frontal camera, bright and warm, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-lilac backdrop with a pale warm-cream floor. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated royal-blue Traditional Chinese glyph 給, the silk component 糸 on the left and the 合 component on the right, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. The lead is an original caped action-figure hero, a chunky plastic toy with a round helmet, a golden belt and a bright red cape three sizes too long that keeps flopping over his own head; a small teddy-bear toy waits at the right with open paws; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the hero strides in, proudly holding a ribbon-tied gift box toward the teddy, and the first spoken 給 lands as his cape swings around and whips the box right out of his hands, the strokes of 糸 appearing as twisted blue threads from the cape's frayed edge. Moment two (1.8-3.4s): the cape flops over his helmet so he walks blindly in a circle, bumping the teddy's foot; the second spoken 給 lands as a second flick of cape snatches the box again and throws it in the air, and the 合 strokes drop in at the right, a blue roof stroke over a small square. Moment three (3.4-5.0s): the hero gets a grin, ties a double knot in the cape's end, and the cape finally obeys, curling down as a neat bow around the gift; the 糸 and 合 click side by side into 給 as he passes the box to the teddy, and the word 給你 is spoken as the teddy pops it open and a cluster of tiny stars bursts out and drifts down. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 給 is completely still, unobstructed and crisp in royal blue; the teddy hugs its gift while the hero strikes a proud pose, the knotted cape fluttering softly behind him, one thumb up, never touching the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「給、給、給你」, read as ㄍㄟˇ、ㄍㄟˇ、ㄍㄟˇ ㄋㄧˇ, first utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 2.8s, the word at about 4.5s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. No background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.

conceptZh: 太空人玩偶想把一顆金星星送給小外星人，可是一走路就飄起來，只好坐上彈簧跳板把自己發射出去。他飛過頭、撞到牆、倒栽蔥掉進水桶，一路撞鬆的線軸和積木落下來排成「給」，星星剛好掉進外星人的飛碟裡：「給你！」
object: a toy spring launcher, a spool of red silk thread, and a stacked tent-roof, bar and crate that get knocked loose when the astronaut toy bonks off the far wall
morph: the launch kicks the spool over and its thread unwinds into 糸 on the left; the wall bonk topples the tent-roof, the bar and the crate so they stack as 合 on the right, and the two halves settle side by side as 給
creativeAngle: 改用「發射」橋段，和前一版披風英雄遞禮物完全不同：主角是會亂飄的太空人玩偶，因為走不過去才把自己彈射出去，飛過頭、撞牆、倒栽蔥進水桶，整段都是大動作。筆畫來自撞擊震落的線軸（糸）和疊好的屋頂、橫桿、箱子（合），結構正確又好讀；「給你」正好落在星星掉進外星人飛碟的瞬間，聲音和畫面同一件事。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated slapstick clip with a locked frontal camera, bright warm lighting, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-mint backdrop with a soft cream floor, nothing busy behind. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated vermilion-red Traditional Chinese glyph 給, the silk component 糸 on the left and the component 合 on the right (a tent-shaped roof over a short horizontal bar over a small square), centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. The lead is an original bouncy astronaut toy: a chubby white plastic figure with a clear fishbowl helmet, a big goofy grin, and boots that keep drifting off the floor at the wrong moment. The only other character is a small green cartoon alien hovering in a toy flying saucer at the far right, holding out both hands hopefully. No real people, no robots.

Moment one (0.0–1.6s): the astronaut stands at the far left hugging a shiny gold star, points eagerly at the alien, and marches toward it, but after two steps its boots float up and it paddles helplessly in mid-air, bumping its helmet on nothing. The first spoken 給 lands at about 0.6s exactly as it points at the alien and holds out the star. It drops back down with a plop onto a red toy spring launcher sitting at the left.

Moment two (1.6–3.2s): the astronaut gets a bright idea, crouches on the launcher in a drumroll pose, counts down on three raised fingers, the spring squashes flat, then BOING: it is flung in one huge arc across the whole frame, the star slipping out of its glove at the top of the arc. The launch kicks a spool of red silk thread off the launcher, and the thread unwinds in the air into the twisted strokes of 糸 on the left of center.

Moment three (3.2–5.0s): the astronaut sails right past the alien, BONKS into a padded bumper wall at the far right with big squash-and-stretch, rebounds backward, flips, and lands upside-down in a tin bucket at the bottom right, boots kicking, helmet wobbling, dazed grin inside. The second spoken 給 lands at about 3.4s exactly on the bonk, as the impact knocks loose a stack beside the wall: a red tent-shaped roof, then a red bar, then a red square crate tumble into the air and drop one on top of the other to form 合 on the right of center. The two halves slide together and settle as a single still, crisp vermilion 給.

Moment four (5.0–8.0s): the glyph 給 stays completely still, unobstructed and readable for the full three seconds. At about 5.0s the alien's wobbly tractor beam catches the falling gold star and lowers it into the saucer dish, and the word 給你 is spoken exactly as the star lands in the alien's hands and the alien hugs it, bouncing with joy. The astronaut, still upside-down in the bucket at the bottom right, pokes one glove out and gives a thumbs-up, its boots doing a tiny happy wiggle; the tractor beam briefly lifts the bucket an inch by mistake and sets it back down with a small bump. Nobody touches or covers the strokes; both characters stay small in the lower corners.

Narration (off-screen only, warm friendly Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, Taiwan standard reading, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「給、給、給你」, read as ㄍㄟˇ、ㄍㄟˇ、ㄍㄟˇ ㄋㄧˇ, first utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 3.4s, the word at about 5.0s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Cartoon bonk and boing sounds only, soft, quieter than the voice. No background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter, no other text of any kind.
